explanation: Fill a reservoir with the first k entries. For the entry at zero-based index i, choose a random position among i+1 possibilities and replace a reservoir slot only when that position is below k. This preserves equal probability for every k-element subset.
timeComplexity: O(n). Every stream entry is inspected once and only k sample entries are retained.
spaceComplexity: O(k). The reservoir holds k values plus counters; stream input storage is not counted as auxiliary.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/online_sampling.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: After t entries, every k-subset has probability 1/C(t,k). Initially t=k and there is only one subset. At the next entry, an old subset survives when no slot is replaced, with probability (t+1−k)/(t+1). A desired subset containing the new entry has t+1−k possible predecessor subsets; each selects the slot of its one extra old entry with probability 1/(t+1). Both cases therefore have probability 1/C(t+1,k), proving uniformity of complete subsets, not merely equal individual inclusion probabilities.
walkthrough: For stream [4,7,9] and k=2, begin with [4,7]. On seeing 9, a uniform draw among 0,1,2 replaces slot 0, replaces slot 1 or leaves the reservoir unchanged. The three resulting subsets are equally likely. JSON arguments are [stream,k]. C++ receives begin/end iterators; Java/Python receive one iterator; C#/JavaScript receive a list. Observed true is distribution validation, not a returned sample.
edgeCases: Sampling the full stream retains every entry.
Each stream position is considered once, without replacement.
